newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Blue chip losses drive Slovak SAX index lower.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip losses drive Slovak SAX index lower.

text.p: Losses to several blue chips drove the SAX index on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) slightly lower in thinner trading on Friday, with brokers predicting low activity for the next few weeks.
Traders said the sluggish mood on the market may have been a knock-on effect from bourses in neighbouring countries, especially sharp declines in the Czech Republic.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta closed down 30 crowns to 1900, with its average price, which is used for calculating the index, down 1.3 percent.
"There is some demand for Nafta shares, but little response from the potential sellers, especially for larger tranches, due to the current low price," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
While Briska said it was difficult to predict developments on the market, flat trading was generally expected to remain in the near future.
"Foreign investors seem to be waiting for a further decline in prices of blue chips before more actively participating on the Slovak market," Briska said.
Slovnaft lost 10 crowns to close at 900, but only two shares were traded.
Steel maker VSZ and the largest commercial bank VUB closed unchanged at 630 and 1,740 crowns respectively.
Overall, volume rose to 464,142 shares, boosted by direct trades, from 163,704 shares traded on Thursday, turnover increased to 667.77 million crowns, from 136.62 million.
